messages.content: I need to work through Nashville next. The board retreat is Wednesday, June 25 through Friday, June 27. Dinner starts downtown at 6:00 Wednesday, Thursday is packed, and we finish at 1:30 Friday. I need flights from Dallas and two hotel nights, but the organizer still hasn't said whether there will be a room block.

I can build this in pieces so the hotel remains changeable. Is the retreat for just you, and do you know the downtown meeting address or at least the venue area? Also, what arrival margin would make the 6:00 p.m. dinner comfortable?
Just me. The meetings are near Fifth and Broadway. I want enough time to get to the hotel, change, and walk or take a very short ride to dinner. I don't need to arrive in the morning.

Then I would target arrival at BNA by about 3:15 p.m. Wednesday. That leaves roughly 45 minutes for a rideshare in normal traffic and close to two hours before dinner. For Friday, a flight after 4:00 p.m. gives you time to leave the meeting at 1:30, retrieve a bag, and reach the airport without making the final session stressful. Should I compare both Love Field and DFW?
Yes. I can use either airport. Nonstop only, and show me totals rather than making the cheapest flight and cheapest hotel look like one option if the times don't actually work together.

Understood. I’ll compare complete two-night combinations using only Wednesday nonstops that arrive by 3:15 and Friday nonstops departing at 4:00 or later. For lodging, should I stay close enough to walk to Fifth and Broadway, or include a less expensive option requiring rides each day?
Include one cheaper hotel if the transportation math still makes sense. The downtown hotels can get ridiculous once taxes and fees show up.

I found three workable flight patterns at the current displayed fares. Flight A uses Love Field both ways: Wednesday 12:05 p.m.–1:50 p.m. and Friday 5:05 p.m.–7:10 p.m., $347 round trip. Flight B uses DFW: Wednesday 12:40 p.m.–2:30 p.m. and Friday 4:35 p.m.–6:45 p.m., $318. Flight C also uses DFW, arriving earlier Wednesday at 12:55 p.m. and returning Friday at 6:20 p.m., $286. All are nonstop and all times are local. The displayed fares include a carry-on but not a checked bag or preferred seat.
C is more airport time than I need on both ends. Keep A and B. What are the hotels?

Near the meeting site, I have the Hyatt Centric Downtown for $684 total after taxes for two nights, about a six-minute walk, with cancellation until 11:59 p.m. on June 23. The Hilton Nashville Downtown is $742 total, roughly three minutes away, cancellable through June 22. The lower-cost comparison is the Holiday Inn Nashville–Vanderbilt at $438 after taxes, but it is about three miles west. I would allow $60–$90 total for rides between that hotel and the retreat over Wednesday evening, Thursday, and Friday.
Does the Hyatt total include any destination fee? And don't count airport rides differently just because one hotel is farther west unless the actual airport fare is meaningfully different.

The Hyatt rate details show $594 in room charges, $90 in taxes, and no separate mandatory destination or facility fee, for $684 total. The Vanderbilt hotel shows $380 plus $58 tax, also with no displayed mandatory fee. Airport transfers should be treated the same for this comparison: about $55–$75 total for BNA rideshares in both directions. The westward difference is too small to justify a separate airport estimate.
Good. Pair A and B with the Hyatt, then pair the cheaper DFW flight with the Vanderbilt hotel. I want the complete numbers.

Combination 1 is Flight A through Love Field plus the Hyatt: $347 airfare + $684 lodging + $55–$75 airport rideshares = $1,086–$1,106. Combination 2 is Flight B through DFW plus the Hyatt: $318 + $684 + $55–$75 = $1,057–$1,077. Combination 3 is Flight B plus the Vanderbilt hotel: $318 + $438 + $55–$75 airport rideshares + $60–$90 retreat transportation = $871–$921. These totals exclude Dallas-side airport transportation, checked baggage, seat purchases, meals, and incidental hotel charges.
So the cheaper hotel saves at least $136 compared with the same flight and Hyatt, even after local rides. Is that right?

Yes. With Flight B, Hyatt is $1,057–$1,077 and Vanderbilt is $871–$921. Comparing the least favorable ends, the Vanderbilt option saves at least $136; depending on actual rideshare prices, the savings could reach $206. The tradeoff is several extra rides and less control over timing on the fully scheduled Thursday.
That makes the Hyatt reasonable for a two-day board schedule. Is there any reason to pay $29 more for Love Field besides which Dallas airport is easier for me?

Not from the Nashville schedule alone. Flight A lands 40 minutes earlier but leaves Nashville 30 minutes later, while Flight B still provides enough margin on both days. The $29 difference mainly buys the Love Field routing. You would want to compare Dallas-side travel time and parking before choosing.
Keep Flight B with the Hyatt as the working plan. But I don't want the uncertain organizer rate to trap me. Can we hold the public hotel rate and switch later?

Yes, provided the final booking screen preserves the June 23 cancellation deadline and does not require a nonrefundable prepayment. Reserve the public flexible rate now, then replace it if the organizer sends a genuinely better block rate. Before switching, compare the block's all-in total, cancellation terms, room type, and whether it carries an early-departure penalty rather than looking only at the nightly price.
Don't book either piece yet. Give me the schedule and the decision points I should send to our operations manager.

Working itinerary: Wednesday, June 25, nonstop DFW–BNA from 12:40 p.m. to 2:30 p.m.; two nights at Hyatt Centric Downtown, checking out Friday, June 27; Friday nonstop BNA–DFW from 4:35 p.m. to 6:45 p.m. Airfare is $318 and lodging is $684 after tax, with no mandatory hotel fee currently displayed. Add $55–$75 for Nashville airport rideshares, for a complete working total of $1,057–$1,077 before Dallas transportation, baggage, seats, meals, and incidentals.
And what exactly remains open while we wait for the organizer?

Operations should verify the exact flight numbers, fare rules, carry-on allowance, and whether the $318 fare is still available before purchase. For the Hyatt, confirm one adult, one room, two nights, the $684 after-tax total, no mandatory destination or facility fee, payment timing, and free cancellation through June 23 at 11:59 p.m. Nashville time. Ask the organizer for the block hotel, booking link or code, all-in two-night total, cutoff date, cancellation deadline, and any early-departure charge. Keep the public Hyatt reservation flexible until those terms arrive; then retain whichever option has the better combination of total cost, location, and cancellation protection. No flight or hotel has been booked.
